transparent.$description: No color: an element that shows whatever is behind it (a secondary or tertiary button at rest).

primary.$description: The page, and the default background of everything that doesn't float.

secondary.$description: One step from primary: side panels, table stripes, a filled card.

tertiary.$description: Two steps from primary: input wells, tracks, code blocks, skeletons.

floating.$description: Anything that floats above the page, with an elevation: menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts. Not for cards: a card sits on the page and uses primary, secondary or tertiary.

inverse.$description: The opposite of primary: tooltips, snackbars.

scrim.$description: Dims the page behind a modal. Always black: a scrim darkens, in both schemes (stronger in dark, where the page is already dark).

disabled.$description: The fill of a disabled control that has one (a disabled primary button, a disabled checked checkbox).

primary.$description: Body text and anything that must read first.

tertiary.$description: The least important text: timestamps, counters. Not for anything the user must read.

placeholder.$description: Placeholder text in inputs; never a label's replacement. Placeholder is text: 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3).

disabled.$description: Text and icons of a disabled element. Exempt from contrast rules (WCAG 1.4.3).

primary.$description: The default edge: dividers, the outline of cards and containers.

secondary.$description: A quieter edge than primary: separation inside a container (menu sections, accordion rows).

strong.$description: An edge that must be seen, 3:1 against the surface: fields, outlined buttons, anything whose edge identifies it.

disabled.$description: The edge of a disabled element.

focus.$description: The focus indicator, on every focusable element: 3:1 against what it surrounds. Its width and offset are focus.ring.

overlay.$description: Hover on neutral backgrounds and tints (white, grays, bg.low, a ghost button). Follows the scheme: darkens in light, lightens in dark.

darken.$description: Hover that always darkens, in both schemes: for a colored or image background you choose to darken.

lighten.$description: Hover that always lightens, in both schemes: for a colored or image background you choose to lighten.

inverse.$description: Hover fill of an inverse element (color.surface.inverse: a neutral primary button): a step off the inverse fill, solid so its contrast is testable.

border.$description: The edge of an interactive element, under the pointer (a field, an interactive card): 3:1 against the surface.

high.$description: Hover fill of a high-emphasis brand element (bg.high: a primary button).

low.$description: Hover fill of a low-emphasis brand element that is transparent at rest (an outlined or ghost button). A solid tint, not an overlay, so content.low's contrast on it is tested.

high.$description: Hover fill of a high-emphasis accent element (bg.high: a primary button).

low.$description: Hover fill of a low-emphasis accent element that is transparent at rest (an outlined or ghost button). A solid tint, not an overlay, so content.low's contrast on it is tested.

high.$description: Hover fill of a high-emphasis critical element (bg.high: a primary button).

low.$description: Hover fill of a low-emphasis critical element that is transparent at rest (an outlined or ghost button). A solid tint, not an overlay, so content.low's contrast on it is tested.

overlay.$description: Pressed on neutral backgrounds and tints (white, grays, bg.low, a ghost button). Follows the scheme: darkens in light, lightens in dark.

darken.$description: Pressed that always darkens, in both schemes: for a colored or image background you choose to darken.

lighten.$description: Pressed that always lightens, in both schemes: for a colored or image background you choose to lighten.

inverse.$description: Pressed fill of an inverse element (color.surface.inverse: a neutral primary button): two steps off the inverse fill.

border.$description: The edge of an interactive element, while pressed (a field, an interactive card): 3:1 against the surface.

high.$description: Pressed fill of a high-emphasis brand element (bg.high: a primary button).

low.$description: Pressed fill of a low-emphasis brand element that is transparent at rest (an outlined or ghost button). A solid tint, not an overlay, so content.low's contrast on it is tested.

bg.$description: The fill of a checked checkbox, the ring and dot of a checked radio: the strongest neutral, 3:1 on the page so the state reads without the brand.

content.$description: The mark on a checked fill (the check, the dash): the page's color, inverted.

bg.$description: The selected option lying on a track (a segment): lighter than the track in both schemes, where surface.floating would be darker than surface.tertiary in dark.

border.$description: The edge of an unchecked checkbox or radio: the strongest neutral, the same as the checked fill (near black on light, near white on dark), so unchecked and checked read as one control. 3:1 against the surface.

bg.$description: The track of an on switch: green, its own value and not the success color, so a design system that changes its feedback palette doesn't change its switches. 3:1 on the page and under a white thumb.

track.$description: The track of an off switch: a mid gray, 3:1 on the page and under a white thumb, so an off switch is findable without an edge on the thumb (WCAG 1.4.11).

thumb.$description: The thumb of a switch, on and off: always white.

border.$description: The edge of an invalid control (a checkbox, a radio, a text field, a chip): 3:1 against the surface, since with the error text it is what says something's wrong (WCAG 1.4.11). The strong critical edge, so it holds when a design system's critical color is light.

busy.$description: Busy: present, not to be disturbed.

bg.$description: A badge's fill: 3:1 on the page, so a dot reads without a number.

content.$description: A badge's count, on its fill.

offset.$description: The gap between an element and its focus ring.

raised.$description: Something lifted within its context: a sticky table cell.

pulse.$description: The faint end of a loading pulse (a skeleton breathing between 1 and this).

xs.$description: Elements up to 16px tall that aren't controls: a small checkbox's box.

sm.$description: Elements up to 20px tall: a checkbox's box, a small tag, a tooltip, a tab's top corners.

md.$description: Elements up to 24px tall: a large checkbox's box, a tag, square avatars.

lg.$description: Elements up to 32px tall that aren't controls: a large tag.

sm.$description: Boxes in the content and small floating layers: cards, alerts, toasts, menus, popovers, a combobox's list.

lg.$description: Large surfaces over the screen: dialogs.

default.$description: The default stroke: dividers, containers, inputs.

strong.$description: An emphasized stroke: selected and focused states.

sm.$description: A 16px icon: in small controls and dense text.

xs.$description: A few words of floating text (a tooltip): 280px.

sm.$description: A short dialog: a confirmation, one question. 400px.

md.$description: A dialog with a form or a paragraph: 560px.

lg.$description: A dialog with a table or a longer form: 720px.

sm.$description: A thin track, inline or in a dense row: 4px.

sm.$description: A 32px picture: in lists and table rows.

md.$description: A 40px picture: next to a name in a header or a card.

lg.$description: A 48px picture: when the picture leads a row or a card.

xl.$description: A 64px picture: the focus of the screen, a profile.

xs.$description: An 8px indicator: a status or a badge's dot on a small avatar, next to body text.

sm.$description: A 12px indicator: a dot on a medium avatar.

md.$description: A 16px indicator: a dot on a large avatar, a small counter.
